20.text: In this way, any reference to common values and to a truth absolutely binding on everyone is lost, and social life ventures on to the shifting sands of complete relativism. At that point, everything is negotiable, everything is open to bargaining: even the first of the fundamental rights, the right to life.
20.notes: Two consecutive sentences of EV 20. Ch. 12 blockquote had spliced EV 22's opening onto these with an ellipsis and printed 'ventures onto' and 'Everything' (capital, without 'At that point,').

22.text: Consequently, when the sense of God is lost, the sense of man is also threatened and poisoned, as the Second Vatican Council concisely states:
22.notes: Opening of EV 22 (not 21). Ch. 12 had cut 'and poisoned'. EV 21 has a different sentence: 'when the sense of God is lost, there is also a tendency to lose the sense of man, of his dignity and his life'.
